plain: Gertrude Ederle, an American swimmer, was the first woman to swim the English Channel, completing the crossing on August 6, 1926. She swam from France to England in 14 hours and 31 minutes, actually beating the existing men's record at the time by nearly two hours, a remarkable achievement given the era's skepticism about women's endurance capabilities. Ederle had already won three Olympic medals, including gold, at the 1924 Paris Games before her Channel swim. Her success significantly boosted public support for women's participation in competitive swimming and endurance sports more broadly, and she returned home to a ticker-tape parade in New York, one of the largest ever given to an athlete at the time.

plain: In top rope climbing, the rope is already anchored at the top of the route, running down to the climber and back up to a belayer on the ground, so a fall results in only a short drop before the rope catches you. In lead climbing, the climber carries the rope up from the ground, clipping it into fixed protection points as they ascend, meaning a fall results in dropping past your last clip point before the rope engages, a longer, more consequential fall. Lead climbing requires more skill, including clipping technique and fall management, and carries higher physical and psychological risk. Top rope is generally considered the safer, more beginner-friendly method, while lead climbing is typically learned only after building solid top rope experience.
